title: Tendulkar Names Ganguly and Dhoni His Favourite Captains in Reddit AMA
excerpt: In a wide-ranging Ask Me Anything, Sachin Tendulkar put Ganguly and Dhoni atop his list — and said his own 1990s captaincy was hampered because he lacked the freedom to pick his team.
body:
• Answering fans in a Reddit Ask Me Anything session on Tuesday, Sachin Tendulkar named Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni as his favourite captains to play under.
  • His verbatim answer: "As far as my favourite captains go, Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni would definitely be at the top of my list!"
  • Asked about his own captaincy, he said he "didn't always have the freedom to pick my team entirely on my own" and that the BCCI today is "a far more professional organisation than it was in the 1990s."
  • The AMA ranged widely: praise for South Africa's Temba Bavuma, a joke for Sanju Samson, and his proposal to split one-day internationals into two innings of 25 overs.

Sachin Tendulkar has never been short of interviewers. On Tuesday he took questions from fans instead, in a Reddit Ask Me Anything session — and one answer settled a pub debate that has run for two decades. Asked to name his favourite captains to have played under, he picked the two men who bookend modern Indian cricket's rise, according to the ANI wire.

"As far as my favourite captains go, Sourav Ganguly and MS Dhoni would definitely be at the top of my list!"

— Sachin Tendulkar, Reddit AMA

The captaincy he didn't control

The sharper answer concerned his own time in charge. Tendulkar captained India in 25 Tests across two stints between 1996 and 2000, and his record — a 16% win rate in Tests — has long been the asterisk on his career. His explanation was pointed. "It was a great honour to lead the team as captain. However, I didn't always have the freedom to pick my team entirely on my own. The BCCI today is a far more professional organisation than it was in the 1990s. Indian cricket also went through a particularly dark phase during that period," he said. He stepped down in March 2000 after a home series defeat to South Africa, and later declined an offer to return as Test captain in 2007 — the job that eventually went to Dhoni.

The rest of the AMA

The session ranged well beyond captaincy. He praised South Africa captain Temba Bavuma — "I truly admire Temba Bavuma's spirit. He has led from the front and delivered some remarkable results for South African cricket" — after the Proteas' 2025 World Test Championship win. Asked about Joe Root closing in on his Test runs record, he said: "I've always rated him very highly and it was evident to me in his first test match that he was going to make it big!" Root stands at 14,278 Test runs, 1,643 short of Tendulkar's 15,921. He repeated his long-standing proposal to split the 50-over ODI into two innings of 25 overs with one ball throughout — "We need to do something before bowlers go extinct" — and, asked what advice he gave Sanju Samson before the T20 World Cup, answered with a Malayalam film joke: "Nee po mone Dinesha!" — adding only that Sanju would explain what it means.

Why the answer matters

Tendulkar played from 1989 to 2013, under captains from Mohammad Azharuddin through Ganguly and Rahul Dravid to Dhoni, scoring 100 international centuries. His verdict carries the weight of the only man who played under all of them: the captain who rebuilt India's self-belief, and the captain who turned it into World Cups, share top billing — while his own tenure, he made clear, was played with one hand tied.
